content.text:
All three renders are done and verified — no overflow, no clipped text, bands full-bleed, columns evenly spaced, photo cropped (never stretched).

**Files in the working folder:**
- `portrait.png` — 1080×1350 (master, scale 1.0)
- `wide.png` — 1200×1000 (scale 0.85)
- `sky.png` — 300×600 (scale 0.28)
- `flyer.html` — the single source template (`?s=` sets the scale)

**How it works:** one template drives all three sizes. Every type size, icon size, gap and padding is `calc(px * var(--s))`, so content scales exactly as specified, while bands (photo, red CTA) use `width:100%` and stay full-bleed at every canvas width. The root is a flex column with `justify-content:space-between`; the photo band is the only flexible element (`flex:1`, `max-height:46%`), so it absorbs the vertical slack that differs between aspect ratios and any remainder spreads evenly between sections. The photo uses `object-fit:cover` with `object-position:50% 72%`, so it crops (keeping the horizon and hills in frame at the wide 3.75:1 crop) rather than distorting.

Verification per size: `scrollHeight == clientHeight` and `scrollWidth == clientWidth` on the root (no overflow), plus a per-element `scrollWidth > clientWidth` check on every text run (headline, names, roles, CTA, steps, footer) — all clean. One fix was made after first inspection: the wide crop initially cut off the horizon, and the photo band was over-capped, so I raised the cap to 46% and moved the crop focus down.
